text:
katie: FYI customer jay is seeing a burst of 502/504s on hosted inference streaming calls for a long multipart prompt. They report failures only during a ~2hr window starting 2025-11-07T14:02:00Z. ticket #INC-9821

jay (customer): hitting 504s mid-stream, we get an empty response body + curl shows 'recv() failed' then timeout. Sample req id: req-8f3c2a1b. Here’s the curl we used: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -H \"Content-Type: multipart/form-data\" --data-binary @big_prompt.json https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream`

omar: can you drop the exact request-id and the edge log lines? also pinging @nora oncall. I’ll check ingress proxy logs (envoy/nginx hop).

katie: attached the edge snippets from customer logs: 
```
[edge-2025-11-07T14:03:12Z] req=req-8f3c2a1b upstream_status=502 upstream_error=\"upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream\" route=hostedapi
[edge-2025-11-07T14:03:12Z] socket_err=104 cause=RST_FROM_UPSTREAM
```

li: deploy-bot shows a model worker rolling update during that window: `deploy-bot: model-embed-v2 rolling update started at 2025-11-07T14:01:58Z on eu-west-1-hostedpool`. Does customer traffic hit that pool?

jay (customer): yes they're in eu-west and we were hitting model-embed-v2 endpoint. We also noticed slow first-token times during the same samples.

omar: hypothesis: long-lived streaming connection + upstream worker bounce during model swap caused the upstream to close streams mid-response, and nginx timed out waiting for the remainder producing 504s for curl clients. Need full edge -> upstream trace to confirm.

nora (oncall): quick mitigation: (1) route customer to a warm fallback model variant for the next hour, (2) increase proxy read_timeout on ingress for long streams for that tenant, (3) temporarily pin traffic to a single warmed worker to avoid rolling swap. We can do (1) and (2) immediately via support console.

li: digging into runtime traces: I see worker process SIGTERM at 14:02:03 then warmup latency spikes (cache miss/kv warmup) causing ~6s of stalled token emission. Proxy had `proxy_read_timeout` set to 5s for streaming endpoints in that pool. So proxy-level timeout > mid-stream stall => client sees 504. Also logs show upstream sent FIN with RST after process exit.

katie: actionables: I’ll (a) enable routing to fallback variant for jay for 1h, (b) request infra to bump streaming proxy_read_timeout to 15s for eu-west hosted pool and (c) ask runtime to stagger model worker rolling updates. Adding notes to ticket INC-9821.

omar: followups for eng: 1) add graceful drain delay to worker shutdown so ongoing streams aren't abruptly closed, 2) make model swap rollout aware of active stream counts and defer if > threshold, 3) add metric for \"stream stall before first token\" to catch warmup-induced stalls.

li: also adding a temporary webhook that marks a worker as \"do-not-rotate\" when it currently has >2 active streams. Will prototype this week.

katie: customer patched to fallback and confirmed success: \"no more 504s in the sample window\" :thumbsup: I’ll keep the ticket open until we have the runtime changes.
thread_summary: Support thread for customer 504s during streaming when model worker rolling update caused upstream closure mid-stream; includes curl sample, edge logs, deploy event, hypotheses, mitigation (fallback routing, bump proxy_read_timeout), and follow-ups for graceful drain and rollout gating.
